fields.h1: Build a Lash Extension Consent Form for Every Set and Fill
fields.hero_description: Build a lash extension consent form clients sign by e-signature, with their eye answers saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Records Before the First Lash
fields.features_subheading: Six parts cover what a lash artist checks before the appointment starts, and each signed copy stays with the client for the next fill.
fields.feature_1:
Eye questions with a box for details

Ask about contact lenses, eye surgery in the last year, and any allergy the client knows of. A yes opens a text box, and the artist reads it before the first lash goes on.
fields.feature_2:
The lash map kept with the signature

Record the style, curl, length, and thickness of each set on the record that holds the signed consent. The next artist opens it before a fill and works from that map.
fields.feature_3:
Each studio policy checked on its own

Put your fill window, removal policy, and late cancellation fee on separate lines with a checkbox each. The record shows which ones the client checked and on what date.
fields.feature_4:
An e-signature before the eye pads go on

Clients sign on their phone from the booking email or on the studio tablet at check-in. The app captures the e-signature and files it with that visit's eye answers and lash map.
fields.feature_5:
No response caps in your busiest month

Book a run of bridal parties in June and every guest still gets a form, since the form has no response caps. Each signed form is a row in a database you own, found by name.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the app's full code to your GitHub repository. Your developer can then place the consent form inside your booking site and host it where the site lives.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Signs When at Four Lash Businesses
fields.tab_content_1:
Each model's form names her student and educator

Every practice model at Bramblecote Lash Academy signs a consent form before a student works on her lashes. It names the student doing the set and the educator watching. Ondine Raskin is the last of Thursday's 8 models to sign. Her record lists student Itzel Valdivieso and educator Margit Ferenczy.
fields.tab_content_2:
For Ravenna's fill, Noor works from the first set's map

Ravenna Gaillard's first set at Juneberry Lash House was hybrid, with a C curl at 10 mm, applied by Tova Brinkerhoff. That lash map went on the record with her signed consent. Three weeks later she books a fill with Noor Haddadi. Before Ravenna arrives, Noor opens the record and starts from the same map.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every bridesmaid signs on her own link before Saturday

Bryony Marchbanks books Plum Hollow Lash Bar for herself and 5 bridesmaids on her Saturday wedding morning. Each of the 6 gets her own consent link and signs for her own lashes. On Thursday, owner Greer Mattingly sees 4 of 6 signed. The app emails a reminder to the other 2, Dagny Kittredge and Camila Rourke.
fields.tab_content_4:
When the set came from elsewhere, only removal is signed

Seabright Lash Studio takes removal bookings for extensions applied elsewhere. Rosario Breckin's set went on 5 weeks ago at another studio, and her form saves when and where. She picks removal only. She signs the removal section, and the full set section stays closed for her visit with Kalani Prieto.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Lash Extension Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to create a lash extension consent form that holds each client's eye answers and lash map.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Copy the questions off your card
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List what your artists record per set
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give each policy its own line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show the wording to a lawyer
fields.howto_step_1_des: If your lash extension consent form is a PDF or a paper card today, copy out each question on it. Then add the eye questions your artists ask out loud at the lash bed, and drop any question nobody reads.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down every note an artist makes after an appointment, down to who applied the set. Each note becomes a field in the lash map. Mark which fields the client answers and which ones the artist completes afterward.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Split your fill window, removal policy, late cancellation fee, and aftercare instructions into short statements with a checkbox each. Short lines read better on a phone than one long paragraph, and the record shows every box the client checked.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Have a lawyer or your insurance agent read the consent wording before any client sees it. Bring their edits back as plain text, and keep a dated copy of each version they sign off on for your own files.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the whole form in a single prompt, section by section, in the order a client meets them. Emergent builds the form along with the database that stores each signed copy. To reword a question after launch, prompt Emergent with the change.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send the link with the booking email
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide when clients get the form. A link in the booking confirmation lets them answer at home, and a reminder the day before reaches anyone who has not signed. If your booking tool has an API, connect it to the app.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a new client booking a full set and a returning client booking a fill through the form. Check that each signature lands on the right client with the answers above it, then publish it and share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a lash extension consent form?
faq_plan.a: A lash extension consent form is what a client signs before an artist applies the first extension. It collects their eye health answers, their agreement to the studio's policies, and a signature. Add the lash map to it as well, and a later artist can match the set.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a lash extension consent form?
faq_plan.a: Start in Emergent's AI form builder with one prompt that describes each section of the form. Emergent returns a working form with its client database. If you already use a lash extension consent form PDF, paste its questions into the prompt. Read the result as a client would, then adjust any question by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What should a lash extension consent form template include?
faq_plan.a: Give it five sections: contact details, eye questions, the lash map, policy checkboxes, and a dated signature. Treat any lash extension consent form template as a first draft, then cut the questions your artists never act on and add the ones they ask out loud.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free lash extension consent form that clients sign online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Send the published link in your booking email, and clients fill in the free lash extension consent form before they arrive. A studio that also does tattoo work can build its tattoo consent form the same way and keep both client lists apart.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead of the appointment should I send a lash extension consent form?
faq_plan.a: Send it the moment the appointment is booked. Clients then answer the eye questions at home instead of at the lash bed, with time to check a medication name or an old surgery date. For walk-ins and anyone who missed the email, hand over the studio tablet at check-in.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep signed lash extension consent forms organized by client?
faq_plan.a: File every signed form under the client it belongs to. In the app Emergent builds, they sit in a database you own, one row per signed form. Search a client's name to see every form they have signed, with the lash map and the policies checked at each visit, newest first.

faq_plan.q: Can a lash extension consent form also cover a lash lift?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the lift gets its own section, since the questions differ. Ask lift clients about their natural lashes and their last lift, and ask extension clients about the set they want. Brow work done with pigment, such as microblading, belongs on a permanent makeup consent form instead.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a lash extension consent form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. In the app Emergent builds, the client signs with a fingertip on their own phone, and the app saves the date beside the e-signature. Ask your lawyer or insurer whether an e-signature covers what your studio needs before you retire paper copies.

faq_plan.q: What should a lash extension consent form say about fills?
faq_plan.a: State your fill window in days and what happens past it, for example that a fill booked after 21 days is priced as a full set. Put it on its own line with a checkbox, and the record shows the client agreed to it before their first set.

faq_plan.q: Can I offer a lash extension consent form in Spanish?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Build the form in both languages and let the client pick one on the first screen, with every answer saved to the same record. Have a fluent speaker check the translated wording before launch. A studio that also waxes brows can reuse the two-language setup for its waxing consent form.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template sellers (Etsy-style Canva files, Amazon pads, a lash supplier's printable), one e-sign template site and two lash blogs that list what a form should say. Each gives a studio a static sheet signed once.
